citation.title: On demand design of two-dimensional phononic crystal bandgap based on machine learning and multi-objective topology optimization
citation.authors: Nansha Gao, Jiacheng Guo, Mou Wang, Yilin Qu, Xingguang Peng, Ye Tang, Xiao Liang, Guang Pan
citation.venue: Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing 242 (issue dated January 2026) 113670 (Crossref; published online 2025-11-26 per the pool record). Hybrid open access, CC BY, per OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar; Crossref licence metadata lists only Elsevier text-mining and STM policy URLs
citation.version_coded: none: only the abstract was read (pool record from OpenAlex). The version of record (ScienceDirect PII S0888327025013718) could not be retrieved by script

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (no accessible full text). Abstract only: VAE, MLP and twin networks predict bandgaps and inverse designs of 2D phononic crystals with five-fold cross-validated accuracy; a twin-network loss balances weight and bandgap targets. No classical comparison.

notes: Access attempts on 2026-09-24, all anonymous with the generic User-Agent and no personal data: (1) doi.org redirects to linkinghub.elsevier.com and ScienceDirect PII S0888327025013718. The article page answered curl with HTTP 403 and a captcha page ('Are you a robot?'), and WebFetch with HTTP 403. No challenge was attempted. (2) Crossref lists only Elsevier text-mining API links (api.elsevier.com), which need an API key; none was used. (3) OpenAlex (W4416683798): hybrid OA, CC BY, publisher version only, any_repository_has_fulltext false. Semantic Scholar lists the DOI as its only open PDF (status HYBRID, licence CCBY). (4) arXiv API: no preprint for title words (phononic + bandgap + demand; phononic + 'twin neural'), the abstract phrase 'twin neural network' with phononic, or the author name Gao Nansha. (5) The CORE search page answered HTTP 403 with a JavaScript and cookie challenge; not pursued. (6) A web search for the exact title found only the ScienceDirect page. Free to read in a browser: yes, per OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar (CC BY hybrid open access), so a human verifier can open it on ScienceDirect. Pointers from the abstract for the verifier: the abstract reports only the method's own five-fold cross-validation accuracy (90% of forward-prediction accuracy values at or above 0.98; 98% of inverse-prediction values at or above 0.95) and names no classical optimizer, run time or cost. The title's 'multi-objective topology optimization' may refer to the twin-network loss that weighs lightweight and bandgap targets [inferred]. At full text, check for a classical TO or genetic-algorithm run, timing or cited result; without one, FT-NOBASELINE applies (or FT-FORWARD if the networks only predict bandgaps and are not used to optimize). Domain: elastic-wave bandgap design of 2D phononic crystals. The task brief flagged FT-DOMAIN (acoustic) as an open scope question; the PROTOCOL §11 clarification dated 2026-09-24 (physics scope: elastic waves) now places elastic-wave and phononic design in solids in scope, with 'acoustic' meaning sound in fluids, so FT-DOMAIN does not apply unless the full text shows fluid acoustics (same area as P00549 and P00605). Duplicate check: no other pool record or prefill with this title or first author. Screening code was I-UNCLEAR. No author named Jun Wang (Mou Wang is a co-author).
